axes.assertion: EpCAM is among the most abundant and consistently expressed epithelial cell-adhesion molecules in colorectal adenocarcinoma, with immunohistochemistry showing strong membranous staining in ~98% of colorectal carcinomas — one of the highest expression frequencies across carcinomas surveyed.

Reports on EpCAM tumor-vs-normal elevation in colorectal cancer are comparator-dependent: EpCAM is intrinsically high in normal colonic epithelium, and while some studies describe overexpression/upregulation in carcinoma relative to distant normal or by protein-level accumulation, adjacent normal mucosa also expresses EpCAM strongly, so tumor-vs-adjacent contrasts are frequently flat.

EpCAM is a bona fide epithelial/carcinoma-intrinsic antigen expressed by the malignant epithelial compartment across the large majority of colorectal tumors and donors, with broadly homogeneous membranous positivity and low frequency of complete antigen loss.

EpCAM is broadly overexpressed across the majority of epithelial carcinomas (colorectal, gastric, pancreatic, breast, prostate, lung and others), establishing it as a pan-carcinoma epithelial marker rather than a colorectal-restricted antigen.

blind_spots.signal: Membranous vs cytoplasmic localization and apical/basolateral polarity of EpCAM in normal vs malignant epithelium — surface accessibility relevant to targeting is a protein-localization readout.
blind_spots.why_omics_blind: Bulk/single-cell RNA and MS abundance cannot resolve subcellular localization or membrane polarity.

blind_spots.signal: Strong EpCAM expression in normal epithelia across many organs (GI tract, biliary, pancreas, lung), the basis of on-target/off-tumor toxicity historically observed with EpCAM-directed agents (e.g. edrecolomab, catumaxomab, adecatumumab).
blind_spots.why_omics_blind: Normal-tissue liability is a therapeutic-window judgment owned by the tumor-selectivity / on-target-safety lenses; the presence lens notes the hand-off but does not adjudicate it.

blind_spots.signal: Prognostic/functional associations of EpCAM expression level with colorectal outcome and clinical response.
blind_spots.why_omics_blind: Clinical/functional outcome is not measurable from the expression/presence omics package.

literature_synthesis.key_divergence: Literature and omics agree EpCAM is abundant, malignant-intrinsic and broadly expressed, but both converge on the same caveat: tumor-vs-normal elevation is not established because EpCAM is intrinsically high in normal colonic and other epithelia — the flat tumor-vs-adjacent contrast reflects a genuine therapeutic-window liability whose verdict belongs to the tumor-selectivity / on-target-safety lenses, not this one.
